title: Verified Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Aiding and Abetting
text: IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE BENJAMIN R. FORTUNE, derivatively on behalf of WESTERN CONSOLIDATED HOLDINGS, INC., Plaintiff, v. BRYANT LAW FIRM, P.C., MARGARET E. CROSS, ANDREW J. HALE, and CLAIRE M. BRYANT, Defendants, and WESTERN CONSOLIDATED HOLDINGS, INC., Nominal Defendant. C.A. No. 2025-0417-KSJM VERIFIED COMPLAINT 1. Plaintiff Benjamin R. Fortune (“Ben” or “Mr. Fortune”), a stockholder of Western Consolidated Holdings, Inc. (“WCH” or the “Company”), brings this derivative action on behalf of the Company against certain officers and directors for breaches of fiduciary duty and against Bryant Law Firm, P.C. for aiding and abetting those breaches. 2. The Company is a Delaware corporation with its principal executive offices at 9824 Meridian Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. Defendant Margaret E. Cross (“Ms. Cross” or “Maggie”) served as the CEO of WCH from 2019 until her resignation in December 2024. Defendant Andrew J. Hale (“Andy” or “Mr. Hale”) served as the CFO of WCH from 2018 to 2024. Defendant Claire M. Bryant (“Ms. Bryant”) is a partner at Bryant Law Firm, P.C., which provided legal advice to the Company during the relevant period. 3. This Court has jurisdiction pursuant to 10 Del. C. § 341. This action concerns a series of self-dealing transactions orchestrated by Ms. Cross and Mr. Hale, with the knowing assistance of Claire Bryant and Bryant Law Firm. 4. On or about March 15, 2023, the Board of WCH approved a stock buyback plan without proper valuation. Ms. Cross caused the Company to purchase 500,000 shares from her brother-in-law’s entity, Peak Capital LLC, at a price of $45 per share, when the fair market value was $28. Mr. Hale, as CFO, certified the financial statements reflecting this transaction as “arm’s length.” Claire Bryant drafted the board consent resolution that omitted material facts. As the Delaware Supreme Court stated in Fortune v. Cross, 312 A.3d 224, 230 (Del. 2024), “directors cannot abdicate their oversight duties.” See also In re WCH S’holder Litig., 202 A.3d 1156, 1170 (Del. Ch. 2019). 5. The operative facts are as follows: a. Ms. Cross’s spouse, Jonathan Cross (not a party), is the managing member of Peak Capital LLC. b. On April 2, 2023, Ms. Cross emailed Mr. Hale: “Andy, we need to push the buyback through before the audit. [Bryant] says the language is clean.” c. Claire Bryant billed 42 hours for drafting the board materials, under billing code 2023-4789 (Policy No. WCH-LEG-9932). Her bar number is 67890 (Delaware Bar). d. The VIN of the Company’s leased vehicle assigned to Ms. Cross is 1HGCM82633A004752. e. Mr. Fortune’s date of birth is December 12, 1970 (12/12/1970). His Social Security number is 987-65-4321. His phone number is (302) 555-0198. His email is ben.fortune@email.com. 6. On June 10, 2023, the Company issued a press release announcing the buyback, quoting Ms. Cross: “This is a great opportunity for our shareholders.” [Cross] knew the statement was false. 7. The Court has personal jurisdiction over all Defendants because each conducted business in Delaware. Claire Bryant maintains an office at 1123 Chancery Lane, Dover, DE 19901. Bryant Law Firm’s registered agent is CT Corporation, 100 W. 10th Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. 8. Count I: Breach of Fiduciary Duty against Margaret E. Cross and Andrew J. Hale. Defendants owed WCH and its stockholders duties of loyalty and care. By causing the Company to overpay for shares from an insider, they breached those duties. They were unjustly enriched. 9. Count II: Aiding and Abetting Breach of Fiduciary Duty against Claire M. Bryant and Bryant Law Firm, P.C. Claire Bryant knowingly assisted the breaches by drafting misleading consents and opining that the transaction was proper. As this Court held in Hale v. WCH Partners, 198 A.3d 674, 689 (Del. Ch. 2018), “an aider and abettor must provide substantial assistance.” 10. WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands judgment against Defendants, jointly and severally, for damages, rescission, disgorgement, pre- and post-judgment interest, costs, and such other relief as the Court deems just. Dated: March 1, 2025 Respectfully submitted, BATES RANGE: FORT001–FORT050 STEVENS & ASSOCIATES By: _______________ Harold J. Stevens (Bar No. 12345) Attorney for Plaintiff Benjamin R. Fortune 111 Commerce Street, Suite 200 Dover, DE 19904 (302) 555-0147 hstevens@stevenslaw.com Nominal Defendant’s address: Western Consolidated Holdings, Inc., 9824 Meridian Street, Wilmington, DE 19801.

title: Excerpt from Verified Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty – Derivative Action
text: IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE CAROLINE M. DANIELS, derivatively on behalf of SOUTHWEST GLOBAL LOGISTICS, INC., Plaintiff, v. ROBERT T. EVANS, LINDA K. PRITCHARD, and McKINLEY & SONS FINANCIAL, LLC, Defendants, and SOUTHWEST GLOBAL LOGISTICS, INC., Nominal Defendant. C.A. No. 2025-0338-MTZ VERIFIED COMPLAINT EXCERPT 1. Plaintiff Caroline M. Daniels (“Carol” or “Ms. Daniels”) is a stockholder of Southwest Global Logistics, Inc. (“SGL” or the “Company”). She brings this derivative action against Robert T. Evans (“Bob” or “Mr. Evans”), the former Chairman; Linda K. Pritchard (“Linda” or “Ms. Pritchard”), the former General Counsel; and McKinley & Sons Financial, LLC (the “Financial Advisor”), for breaches of fiduciary duty and for unjust enrichment. 2. The Company is a Delaware corporation headquartered at 4500 Industrial Parkway, Newark, DE 19702. Defendant Evans resides at 12 Elm Lane, Wilmington, DE 19808. Defendant Pritchard resides at 89 Oak Street, Dover, DE 19904. McKinley & Sons Financial maintains its principal place of business at 200 Market Street, Philadelphia, PA 19103. 3. This Court has subject matter jurisdiction under 8 Del. C. § 225 and 10 Del. C. § 342. 4. In 2022, the Company entered into a consulting agreement with McKinley & Sons Financial, paying $2.5 million for a fairness opinion that was never delivered. Mr. Evans and Ms. Pritchard approved the payment without obtaining any work product. As the Delaware Supreme Court held in Evans v. Daniels, 289 A.3d 453, 467 (Del. 2024), “a fiduciary cannot approve a payment for no consideration.” See also Pritchard v. SGL Investors, 195 A.3d 789, 801 (Del. Ch. 2018). 5. Ms. Daniels’s date of birth is May 5, 1981 (5/5/1981). Her Social Security number is 444-55-6666. Her phone number is (302) 555-0234. Her email is caroline.daniels@sglshareholder.com. 6. On January 12, 2023, Mr. Evans sent an email to Linda Pritchard stating: “Bob – get [McKinley] to sign the engagement letter. We need the cover.” [Evans] later admitted in his deposition that no work was performed. 7. Bates Range: SGL001–SGL100. Policy No. SGL-INS-2022-7843. The Company’s vehicle assigned to Mr. Evans has VIN 5XYZU3LA7DG123456. 8. Ms. Pritchard’s Delaware Bar Number is 55432. McKinley & Sons Financial’s CEO is named Thomas McKinley, who is not a party. 9. Count I: Breach of the Duty of Loyalty against Robert T. Evans and Linda K. Pritchard. Defendants placed their interests ahead of the Company by authorizing a fraudulent payment to an entity with which Evans had a prior relationship. 10. Count II: Aiding and Abetting Breach of Fiduciary Duty against McKinley & Sons Financial, LLC. The Financial Advisor knew the opinion was not prepared but accepted the fee. WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands judgment against Defendants, jointly and severally, for damages in excess of $2.5 million, equitable relief, and costs. Dated: March 5, 2025 Respectfully submitted, COASTLINE LEGAL GROUP By: _______________ Angela M. Russo (Bar No. 33456) Attorney for Plaintiff Caroline M. Daniels 2000 Delaware Avenue, Suite 500 Wilmington, DE 19806 (302) 555-0456 arusso@coastlinelegal.com

title: Verified Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Waste of Corporate Assets
text: IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE SUSAN M. THORNTON, derivatively on behalf of NORTH ATLANTIC ENERGY CORP., Plaintiff, v. DAVID R. MYERS, JENNIFER L. WATSON, and HARRISON & HARRISON MANAGEMENT, LLC, Defendants, and NORTH ATLANTIC ENERGY CORP., Nominal Defendant. C.A. No. 2025-0459-LWW VERIFIED COMPLAINT 1. Plaintiff Susan M. Thornton (“Sue” or “Ms. Thornton”) is a stockholder of North Atlantic Energy Corp. (“NAE” or the “Company”). She brings this derivative action against David R. Myers (“Dave” or “Mr. Myers”), the former CEO; Jennifer L. Watson (“Jenny” or “Ms. Watson”), the former Chief Operating Officer; and Harrison & Harrison Management, LLC (the “Management Consultant”), for gross breaches of fiduciary duty, corporate waste, and unjust enrichment. 2. The Company is a Delaware corporation with its principal offices at 7800 Coastal Highway, Lewes, DE 19958. Defendant Myers resides at 34 Bayview Drive, Rehoboth Beach, DE 19971. Defendant Watson resides at 112 Pine Street, Milton, DE 19968. Harrison & Harrison Management is a Delaware limited liability company with its registered office at 300 S. State Street, Dover, DE 19901. 3. This Court has jurisdiction under 10 Del. C. § 341 and 8 Del. C. § 327. 4. In 2023, the Company hired Harrison & Harrison Management to provide operational consulting at a cost of $1.8 million. The consultant’s principal, George Harrison (no relation to the firm’s name), is Mr. Myers’s college roommate. The contract was awarded without competitive bidding. No deliverables were provided. As the Delaware Supreme Court noted in Myers v. Thornton, 298 A.3d 542, 550 (Del. 2024), “a fiduciary cannot waste corporate assets on a sham contract.” See also Watson v. NAE S’holders, 201 A.3d 876, 888 (Del. Ch. 2020). 5. Ms. Thornton’s date of birth is September 14, 1978 (9/14/1978). Her Social Security number is 123-45-6789. Her phone number is (302) 555-0789. Her email is sue.thornton@naeinvestor.com. 6. On March 1, 2023, Mr. Myers sent a text to Ms. Watson: “Jenny, tell [Harrison] the fee is fine. No need for a RFP.” [Myers] later deleted the text, but it was recovered from Company servers. 7. Bates Range: THOR001–THOR075. Policy No. NAE-POL-2023-5521. The Company’s leased vehicle assigned to Mr. Myers has VIN 2C3CDXBG9PH123456. 8. Mr. Myers’s Delaware Bar Number (he is a licensed attorney, inactive) is 87654. Ms. Watson is not an attorney. Harrison & Harrison Management is wholly owned by George Harrison. 9. Count I: Breach of the Duty of Loyalty and Waste against David R. Myers. Defendant Myers caused the Company to enter into a sham contract for personal benefit. 10. Count II: Breach of the Duty of Loyalty against Jennifer L. Watson. Defendant Watson approved the contract without due diligence. 11. Count III: Aiding and Abetting against Harrison & Harrison Management, LLC. The consultant received payment knowing no services would be rendered. WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands judgment against Defendants, jointly and severally, for damages, rescission of the contract, disgorgement of fees, and costs. Dated: March 10, 2025 Respectfully submitted, EASTERN SHORE LEGAL, P.A. By: _______________ Katherine L. O’Brien (Bar No. 76543) Attorney for Plaintiff Susan M. Thornton 101 N. Dupont Highway, Suite 3 Dover, DE 19901 (302) 555-0321 kobrien@easternshorelegal.com

title: Verified Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Unjust Enrichment
text: IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE THOMAS J. FISCHER, derivatively on behalf of MID-ATLANTIC BIOTECH, INC., Plaintiff, v. VICTORIA H. KLEIN, PAUL D. GRAYSON, and KLEIN ASSOCIATES CONSULTING, LLC, Defendants, and MID-ATLANTIC BIOTECH, INC., Nominal Defendant. C.A. No. 2025-0512-FJJ VERIFIED COMPLAINT 1. Plaintiff Thomas J. Fischer (“Tom” or “Mr. Fischer”) is a stockholder of Mid-Atlantic Biotech, Inc. (“MAB” or the “Company”). He brings this derivative action against Victoria H. Klein (“Vicky” or “Ms. Klein”), the former Chief Scientific Officer; Paul D. Grayson (“Paul” or “Mr. Grayson”), the former Chief Financial Officer; and Klein Associates Consulting, LLC (the “Consulting Entity”), for breaches of fiduciary duty and unjust enrichment. 2. The Company is a Delaware corporation with its principal executive offices at 5500 Innovation Drive, Newark, DE 19711. Defendant Klein resides at 7 Harvard Lane, Wilmington, DE 19809. Defendant Grayson resides at 22 Chestnut Court, Hockessin, DE 19707. Klein Associates Consulting is a Delaware LLC with its registered address at 1000 N. Market Street, Suite 400, Wilmington, DE 19801. 3. This Court has jurisdiction under 10 Del. C. § 341. 4. In 2023, the Company paid $4.2 million to Klein Associates Consulting for “strategic advisory services.” The consulting entity is wholly owned by Victoria Klein’s spouse, Mark Klein (not a party). Mr. Grayson, as CFO, approved the payment without a written contract. The Delaware Supreme Court, in Klein v. Fischer, 315 A.3d 411, 419 (Del. 2024), stated: “A fiduciary must avoid conflicts of interest.” See also Grayson v. MAB S’holders, 204 A.3d 567, 579 (Del. Ch. 2021). 5. Mr. Fischer’s date of birth is March 3, 1972 (3/3/1972). His Social Security number is 789-12-3456. His phone number is (302) 555-0678. His email is tom.fischer@mabholder.com. 6. On July 15, 2023, Ms. Klein emailed Mr. Grayson: “Paul, route the payment to [Klein Associates]. Mark needs the funds.” [Klein] made no disclosure to the Board. 7. Bates Range: FISC001–FISC090. Policy No. MAB-INS-2023-1122. The Company’s vehicle assigned to Ms. Klein has VIN 1N4AL3AP2DN123456. 8. Ms. Klein’s Delaware Bar Number is 44556 (she is a licensed patent attorney). Mr. Grayson’s Bar Number is 77889 (inactive). Klein Associates Consulting’s EIN is 11-2223333. 9. Count I: Breach of the Duty of Loyalty against Victoria H. Klein. Defendant Klein caused the Company to overpay an entity in which she had a personal interest. 10. Count II: Breach of the Duty of Care against Paul D. Grayson. Defendant Grayson failed to review the transaction before authorizing payment. 11. Count III: Unjust Enrichment against Klein Associates Consulting, LLC. The Consulting Entity received funds without providing commensurate value. WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands judgment against Defendants, jointly and severally, for damages, disgorgement, and costs. Dated: March 15, 2025 Respectfully submitted, PIEDMONT LEGAL GROUP, P.C. By: _______________ Steven A. Parker (Bar No. 22334) Attorney for Plaintiff Thomas J. Fischer 200 W. 9th Street, Suite 100 Wilmington, DE 19801 (302) 555-0987 sparker@piedmontlegal.com

title: Verified Complaint for Breach of Fiduciary Duty and Misappropriation of Trade Secrets
text: IN THE COURT OF CHANCERY OF THE STATE OF DELAWARE JASON M. LEWIS, derivatively on behalf of CENTRAL COAST PHARMACEUTICALS, INC., Plaintiff, v. ANGELA D. RICHARDS, CHRISTOPHER J. BOOTH, and BOOTH CAPITAL PARTNERS, LP, Defendants, and CENTRAL COAST PHARMACEUTICALS, INC., Nominal Defendant. C.A. No. 2025-0581-SK VERIFIED COMPLAINT 1. Plaintiff Jason M. Lewis (“Jay” or “Mr. Lewis”) is a stockholder of Central Coast Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (“CCP” or the “Company”). He brings this derivative action against Angela D. Richards (“Angie” or “Ms. Richards”), the former Chief Technology Officer; Christopher J. Booth (“Chris” or “Mr. Booth”), the former CEO; and Booth Capital Partners, LP (the “Investment Fund”), for breaches of fiduciary duty and misappropriation of trade secrets. 2. The Company is a Delaware corporation with its principal place of business at 8900 Research Boulevard, Wilmington, DE 19803. Defendant Richards resides at 55 Ocean View Road, Dewey Beach, DE 19971. Defendant Booth resides at 1000 Brandywine Drive, Wilmington, DE 19807. Booth Capital Partners is a Delaware limited partnership with its principal office at 1201 Pennsylvania Avenue, Suite 800, Wilmington, DE 19806. 3. This Court has jurisdiction under 10 Del. C. § 341 and 8 Del. C. § 225. 4. In 2022, Mr. Booth and Ms. Richards formed Booth Capital Partners to acquire a competing drug formulation developed by Ms. Richards while she was employed at CCP. They used confidential CCP data to launch a rival product. As the Delaware Supreme Court held in Richards v. Lewis, 301 A.3d 634, 645 (Del. 2024), “a fiduciary must not exploit corporate opportunities for personal gain.” See also Booth v. CCP S’holders, 199 A.3d 1023, 1035 (Del. Ch. 2019). 5. Mr. Lewis’s date of birth is August 8, 1985 (8/8/1985). His Social Security number is 555-66-7777. His phone number is (302) 555-0123. His email is jason.lewis@ccpinvestor.com. 6. On February 10, 2022, Ms. Richards emailed Mr. Booth: “Chris, I have the formula. [Booth Capital] can fund the patent.” [Richards] copied the files despite the Company’s confidentiality policy. 7. Bates Range: LEWI001–LEWI110. Policy No. CCP-IP-2022-3344. The Company’s vehicle assigned to Mr. Booth has VIN 1G1ZD5ST1LF123456. 8. Ms. Richards’s Delaware Bar Number is 66789 (in-house counsel). Mr. Booth’s Bar Number is 33445. Booth Capital Partners has no separate counsel of record. 9. Count I: Breach of the Duty of Loyalty and Misappropriation against Angela D. Richards. Defendant Richards misappropriated CCP’s proprietary drug formula. 10. Count II: Breach of the Duty of Loyalty and Aiding and Abetting against Christopher J. Booth. Defendant Booth facilitated the misappropriation and funded the rival venture. 11. Count III: Aiding and Abetting against Booth Capital Partners, LP. The Fund knowingly used the stolen formula. WHEREFORE, Plaintiff demands judgment against Defendants, jointly and severally, for damages, an accounting, injunctive relief, and costs. Dated: March 20, 2025 Respectfully submitted, COASTAL LEGAL SERVICES, LLC By: _______________ Michael R. Donovan (Bar No. 99887) Attorney for Plaintiff Jason M. Lewis 5 Market Street Plaza, Suite 200 Dover, DE 19901 (302) 555-0765 mdonovan@coastallegalservices.com
